title: Working notes: kernel vs scheduler knobs (Hardware tuning profiles pack)
content:
Context
- This is a scratchpad for the “Hardware tuning profiles pack” effort (H100 / L40S / B200). The goal is to list candidate knobs, hypotheses for why they help/hurt, and who owns measurement + implementation. This doc is intentionally messy.
- Audience: Runtime (kernel + scheduling), Perf/Applied ML, SRE/Infra.

What we’re trying to separate
- “Kernel knobs” = what kernel implementation or variant we run for core ops (attention, GEMM paths, fused kernels), plus compile/dispatch selection and fallback behavior.
- “Scheduler knobs” = how we batch and queue work (prefill vs decode prioritization, admission control, queue limits, batch composition policies).
- There are interactions (e.g., batch shape influences kernel choice; kernel speed changes queue dynamics).

Assumptions / baseline (as of runtime-1.22 workstream)
- H100: generally compute-rich; tail latency regressions we’ve seen have been from batching policies + mixed workloads rather than kernel throughput alone.
- L40S: more memory-sensitive under burst + mixed long contexts; risk = OOM / fragmentation and “death by queueing” when concurrency too high.
- B200: early access; primary risk is compatibility drift (driver/CUDA, kernel fallback rates). We must gate unsafe defaults.

Knobs inventory (candidate list)

A) Scheduler / batching / queueing knobs
1) Workload bucket definition
- Knob: bucket boundaries for (prompt_len, expected_decode_len, streaming/non-streaming, tool-calls?)
- Hypothesis: better buckets reduce head-of-line blocking and avoid p99 spikes when long prefill enters a decode-heavy queue.
- Risk: too many buckets increases complexity + potential config drift; too few buckets fails to capture long-context behavior.
- Owner: Marcus Reed (bucket definitions + bench), Sofia Ivanova (policy), Claire Dubois (methodology review)
- Related: github:redwood#24895 (workload buckets + queue prioritization)

2) Prefill vs decode prioritization policy
- Knob: prefill_weight, decode_weight, and/or max_prefill_inflight; “decode-first” mode toggle
- Hypothesis: decode-first improves p95/p99 for chatty streaming workloads; but can hurt throughput on pure completion workloads.
- Failure mode: starvation of prefill under sustained decode, leading to queue growth and eventual timeout bursts.
- Owner: Sofia Ivanova + Julian Moore (instrumentation)

3) Continuous batching: max_batch_tokens / max_batch_size / max_wait_ms
- Knob: upper bounds and waiting strategy per SKU
- Hypothesis: aggressive max_wait_ms improves throughput but creates p99 tail under mixed prompt sizes; needs SKU-specific cap.
- Known issue: p99 regression observed in Hosted canary from overly aggressive batching default; reverted in hotfix.
- Owner: Lena Fischer (implementation), Marcus Reed (bench), SRE review: Sean Gallagher
- Related: github:redwood#24988 (hotfix revert aggressive batching default)

4) Batch composition rule: “shape-aware packing”
- Knob: prefer similar prompt_len groupings vs greedily pack tokens
- Hypothesis: shape-aware packing reduces kernel jitter and improves predictability; but might lower utilization on sparse traffic.
- Open question: is this worth complexity vs just better max_wait_ms + queue limits?
- Owner: Sofia (decision), Noah Patel (architecture sanity check)

5) Admission control / queue limits
- Knob: max_queue_depth, max_inflight_requests, sku-specific “safe inflight tokens” limit
- Hypothesis: explicit queue bounds prevent overload cascades and keep tail lat manageable.
- Risk: rejects can show up as 429/503; needs coordination with product/SLO definitions.
- Owner: Lena (impl), SRE: Rafael Mendes, Product input: Lauren Bishop
- Related: github:redwood#25003 (profile-aware admission control)

6) Backpressure semantics (streaming)
- Knob: per-connection token rate smoothing; how we count “active” streams
- Hypothesis: smoothing avoids microbursts that trigger queue oscillations.
- Open question: do we have enough observability to debug this in the field? (need queueing vs compute separation)
- Owner: Julian Moore + Allison Grant (metrics)
- Related: github:redwood#25063 (separate queueing vs compute time in traces)

7) Concurrency caps (especially L40S)
- Knob: default concurrency per model size bucket; cap inflight KV size
- Hypothesis: L40S needs conservative defaults to avoid fragmentation and OOM under burst traffic.
- Observed: intermittent OOM on L40S pool under burst traffic (see ticket trail). Most correlated with long-context + high concurrency.
- Owner: Omar El-Sayed + Samir Qureshi (memory), Lena (scheduler tie-in)
- Related: github:redwood#24918 (L40S caps), github:redwood#25071 (adjust L40S KV cache headroom)


B) Kernel selection / dispatch knobs
1) Attention kernel variant selection (H100)
- Knob: attention_kernel=v2/v3; thresholds for selecting v3 (context length, head dim, dtype, quantization mode)
- Hypothesis: v3 improves throughput on mid/long context but may have fallback/edge cases; needs deterministic selection and telemetry.
- Known: microbench shows v3 wins in steady-state but had a long-context edge case where fallback rate spiked.
- Owner: Hiro Tanaka (lead), Grace Kim (implementation), Isabella Rossi (microbench), Yuki Sato (selection + fallbacks)
- Related: github:redwood#24911 (H100 attention kernel v3 + fallback rules)

2) Kernel fallback behavior
- Knob: when to fall back (OOM risk? unsupported shape? driver mismatch?), and whether fallback is “hard” (fail load) vs “soft” (slower kernel)
- Hypothesis: soft fallback preserves uptime but can silently kill SLOs; need counters + alerts.
- Requirement: export kernel_choice and kernel_fallback counters labeled by (profile_id, sku, model, reason)
- Owner: Yuki Sato (telemetry + policy), Allison Grant (dashboards)
- Related: github:redwood#24911, slack:eng-platform/1768965000 (alert tuning)

3) GEMM / fused MLP kernel path
- Knob: enable_fused_mlp, use_tensor_cores_strict, algo selection for FP8/BF16
- Hypothesis: for H100/B200, fused paths stabilize latency; for L40S, memory traffic dominates and fused may not help.
- Open question: do we have enough reproducibility given driver/CUDA heterogeneity? (esp. B200 early)
- Owner: Hiro + Noah

4) Compilation/cache settings
- Knob: compilation_cache_size, warmup plan, precompile set
- Hypothesis: reduces p99 on cold starts and model reloads, but increases memory footprint.
- Interaction: runtime selection logic needs to avoid profile mismatch across GPU pools when model reload happens.
- Owner: Noah Patel (architecture), Quentin Harris (compat matrix)
- Related: github:redwood#24958 (prevent profile mismatch on model reload)

5) Quantization interactions
- Knob: quant_mode (FP8/INT8/none) + kernel compatibility constraints
- Hypothesis: quantization changes optimal batching and sometimes changes fallback thresholds.
- Need: performance + quality guardrails; at minimum ensure profiles don’t select kernels that silently disable quant.
- Owner: Arjun Desai (quant/perf), Jonas Weber (evals sign-off)


C) Memory / KV cache knobs (cross-cutting; impacts both kernel + scheduler)
1) KV cache headroom / reservation
- Knob: kv_cache_reserved_gb or reserved_pct; also “min_free_mem_gb” guardrail
- Hypothesis: fixed headroom reduces OOM and fragmentation; too conservative hurts throughput.
- Per-SKU: L40S should reserve more; H100 can be tighter but still needs buffer for spikes.
- Owner: Omar El-Sayed + Samir Qureshi
- Related: github:redwood#24902 (compaction thresholds + counters), github:redwood#25071

2) Compaction thresholds / cadence
- Knob: compaction_trigger_pct, compaction_max_ms, compaction_cooldown_s
- Hypothesis: compaction reduces fragmentation but steals time from decode under load (can show as p99 spikes).
- Observability needed: compaction_time_ms, fragmentation_estimate, and correlation with scheduler_queue_ms.
- Owner: Omar (metrics), Sofia (policy: when compaction is allowed)

3) Allocator behavior
- Knob: allocator type + growth strategy; large-page/hugepages guidance (where applicable)
- Hypothesis: allocator tuning is mostly about avoiding pathological fragmentation on L40S; H100 less sensitive.
- Open question: how much can we control in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Need “required vs best-effort” split.
- Owner: Samir + Irene Choi (fleet constraints)


Current hypotheses (to validate with benchmarks)
H1: p99 regressions we’ve seen are scheduler-driven, not kernel-driven
- Test: keep kernels fixed; vary batching/max_wait_ms + workload buckets.
- Expected: p99 sensitivity larger to scheduler than kernel variant.
- Owner: Marcus + Isabella

H2: Kernel v3 on H100 reduces mean latency but increases tail under long contexts if fallback conditions aren’t tight
- Test: long-context bucket sweep; measure kernel_fallback_rate + p99.
- Expected: if fallback rate > ~1% in steady-state, p99 will degrade even if p50 improves.
- Owner: Hiro + Yuki

H3: L40S stability requires explicit concurrency caps + KV headroom; otherwise OOM/fragmentation presents as “random” tail latency
- Test: L40S burst traffic profile with long prompt distribution; vary kv headroom and max inflight.
- Expected: with caps + headroom, OOMs go to ~0 and tail becomes predictable; throughput drops modestly.
- Owner: Omar + Lena

H4: Admission control based on “inflight KV estimate” beats naive request-count limits
- Test: compare request-count cap vs inflight-token/KV cap on mixed lengths.
- Expected: fewer p99 spikes at similar rejection rate.
- Owner: Lena


Measurement: what we MUST log/graph for every profile run
- scheduler_queue_ms (separate from compute)
- prefill_ms, decode_ms (p50/p95/p99)
- tokens/sec (prefill + decode separately if possible)
- kernel_choice (label = kernel_id)
- kernel_fallback_count + reason
- kv_cache_hit_rate (if applicable), kv_allocated_gb, kv_free_gb
- fragmentation_estimate + compaction_time_ms
- OOM count, retry count, rejected_requests count (admission control)
- GPU util, SM occupancy, HBM bandwidth proxy if available

Allison: please make sure dashboard panels can segment by profile_id AND sku without blowing up cardinality. Prefer top-K models or aggregate by model_family.


Early benchmark notes (Jan–Feb 2026; messy)
- H100 results (drive:…/h100-results-jan-2026)
  - Attention v3: +6–10% throughput on mid-context buckets; best gains when batch has similar sequence lengths.
  - Tail: two runs showed p99 regressions on long-context bucket; correlated with kernel fallback spikes and increased scheduler queueing.
  - Takeaway: need tighter v3 selection thresholds + fallback alerts.

- L40S results (drive:…/l40s-results-jan-2026)
  - Stable region: concurrency <= (TBD per model size) with higher KV headroom; beyond that, OOM/fragmentation rises quickly.
  - Compaction: aggressive compaction reduces OOM but adds latency spikes if it runs during heavy decode.
  - Takeaway: L40S profile should be conservative by default; allow overrides only with guardrails.

- B200 smoke (drive:…/b200-smoke-results-feb-2026)
  - Biggest issue is driver/CUDA mismatch causing elevated fallback rate; performance data is not trustworthy until baseline is standardized.
  - Takeaway: hard compatibility gate and explicit opt-in profile version pin (no “auto” defaults).


Owner assignments / TODOs (next 2 weeks)
- Sofia: finalize first cut of scheduler knobs that go into profile schema (avoid “too many knobs” v1). Define which knobs are “tunable” vs “locked” per deployment mode.
- Hiro + Grace: define attention kernel selection conditions (v3) + fallback reasons taxonomy.
- Yuki: ensure kernel_choice + fallback counters are emitted everywhere; confirm label set.
- Omar + Samir: pick L40S KV headroom defaults and compaction policy; define “stop-the-world compaction” safety rules.
- Marcus: propose benchmark matrix slices that exercise mixed workloads (short + long prompts) explicitly.
- Allison: dashboard draft for profile adoption + p95/p99 deltas by profile; include alert suggestions for fallback rates.


Open questions / arguments we still haven’t settled
- Should the profile choose “prefill-first vs decode-first” or should that be a runtime default independent of profile?
- How do we handle low-traffic periods where shape-aware packing hurts latency (waiting for similar shapes)? Do we need a “traffic-aware” mode?
- For Dedicated customers, do we allow pinning individual knob overrides or only pin full profile_version/profile_id? (Product prefers pin-by-version; runtime wants limited overrides with audit.)
- Compatibility matrix: do we key by (SKU + driver + CUDA) only, or also include firmware / PCIe vs SXM vs MIG? Infra says MIG is mostly off in Hosted but may exist in Private.
- Metric cardinality: profile_id x model x region may be too high; need strategy.


Notes to self / cleanup
- This doc should eventually be split into:
  - (1) profile schema and selection rules (Confluence)
  - (2) expected behavior per SKU (Confluence)
  - (3) internal tuning notes (keep in Drive)
